title: Software management
subtitle: APT, apt-get, apt-cache, and package families — flip for meaning, example, and notes

cards.meaning: Package = software in an archive; PMS installs, upgrades, configures, and removes packages (and deps)
cards.example: Install a package instead of copying random binaries onto a server
cards.notes: The manager tracks files, versions, and dependencies.
Interview hook: yum is to rpm as apt is to dpkg. Low-level = single file; high-level = repos + deps.

cards.meaning: Low-level talks to one file on disk; high-level talks to repositories, resolves deps, then calls low-level
cards.example: rpm -i foo.rpm  ·  dpkg -i foo.deb  ·  apt-get install nginx
cards.notes: Newer RHEL uses dnf; this course names yum.

cards.meaning: Retrieve new lists of packages from repos (refresh the catalog)
cards.notes: Does not upgrade installed software by itself. Run after adding a repo or APT will not see new packages.
Memory hook: update = refresh catalog; upgrade/install = change what is on disk.

cards.meaning: Install by package name, not the .deb filename
cards.notes: High-level apt-get downloads and resolves deps; you name the package (libc6), not the file (libc6.deb).

cards.meaning: Remove the package; config files may stay
cards.notes: Opposite of install for the binaries; configs can remain on disk.

cards.meaning: Remove the package and its config files
cards.notes: remove keeps configs; purge does not.

cards.meaning: Verify there are no broken dependencies
cards.notes: Diagnostic — does not install or upgrade by itself.

cards.meaning: apt-get changes the system; apt-cache only looks up the binary cache
Regex search · readable record · general info · raw dependency list
Where APT reads repository lists (main file + per-vendor drop-ins)
cards.notes: Extra vendors (Docker, Terraform, …) drop a file in sources.list.d/. Then apt-get update.

cards.meaning: Binary packages from a mirror for a release and component set
cards.example: deb http://ftp.by.debian.org/debian/ buster main non-free contrib
cards.notes: deb-src = source packages. buster = Debian 10 codename. main/contrib/non-free = components.

cards.meaning: Debian binary package extension; “Deb” from Debra (Ian Murdock’s partner) / Debian
cards.notes: APT is the user interface + libraries that install and remove software on Debian and variants (Ubuntu, Mint, …).
